question: Does the M-body STAGED/5000 ns candidate remain preferable to DIRECT/5000 ns across the established two-source and one-source eight-E-core high-contention geometries?

retained.role: Phase 14 anchor; carry forward without pooling

requiredCalculations: For each new source topology separately, compute block-paired STAGED-minus-DIRECT throughput effects with mean, median, sample standard deviation, range, percentage delta, and win count.
Report treatment means and sample CV across the eight independent JVM replicas for every new action/topology combination.
Report within-replica CV without treating measurement iterations as independent forks.
Carry the four-source Experiment 30 DIRECT/5000 ns versus STAGED/5000 ns result forward as retained evidence; do not pool its replicas with Experiment 34.
Report measured contention and productiveHandleRatio for every action/topology treatment. Source count is a fixture control, not the final physical variable.

Place the new and retained treatments against the intended 65-80%, 80-90%, 90-97%, and 97-100% high-contention regions using measured contention, and state explicitly which regions are actually covered.
Evaluate acquisition success, contention movement, idle fraction, and throughput jointly, allowing policy-induced state movement to remain part of the treatment effect.
Classify every state-22-dominant measurement while retaining throughput as the primary ranking metric.
interpretationRules: Do not infer physical contention from source count alone; use measured contention and productiveHandleRatio.
Do not compare raw throughput across source topologies as though source count were the treatment of interest; compare STAGED against DIRECT within each topology.

If STAGED is repeatably preferable at one, two, and the retained four sources, treat the E-core candidate as portable across the measured covered region and proceed to representative P-core verification.
If a topology changes or makes the action winner ambiguous, preserve that topology-specific split and refine only the affected action/idle region before P-core verification.
If the fixtures fail to cover representative parts of the 65-100% physical contention range, name only the smallest additional retained geometry needed to fill the observed gap.
Do not reopen skip unless a narrow action crossover repeatedly fails to settle.
Do not tune contention thresholds, add a state-22 escape policy, or average contradictory topologies.
stopRule: Stop after classifying E-core contention/topology sensitivity and naming the minimum representative P-core verification or smallest missing E-core fixture. Do not configure or execute P-core, skip, or threshold work.
